exposure: Uterine rupture at the site of a previous caesarean scar
abnormal placental penetration through the uterus wall with bladder invasion
cohort: A single patient with uterine rupture at the site of a previous cesarean scar with abnormal placental penetration through the uterus wall with bladder invasion at 21 weeks of gestation.
finding: Uterine rupture with placenta percreta invading the urinary bladder is a rare but serious pregnancy complication that can lead to thrombotic microangiopathy and necessitate immediate intervention.
mod_finding: The study reports a case of uterine rupture at the site of a previous cesarean scar, highlighting the risk associated with this delivery history.
